resources.string: This queue of characters enters the compiler. Which phase works on it first? Tap it.
It is the phase that joins letters into words.
Lexical. It is first on the belt, and its output feeds the syntax phase.
Using a variable that was never declared. Which phase reports that error? Tap it.
The tokens exist and the order is right. What is missing is meaning.
Semantic. The sentence has the right form, but the name does not exist.
Now look for E on the right side of the rules. Which terminal comes right after it? Tap it.
Look at the rule for T. Where does E appear?
The closing parenthesis. In open parenthesis, E, close parenthesis, it comes right after E.
X goes to plus T X. In which cell of the X row does this rule go? Tap it.
Look at the first symbol of the right side.
In the plus column, the FIRST of that right side.
Tap every cell that says to shift.
Shift is the letter s with the state number.
Those three. Each s comes from an automaton arrow on a terminal.
First round: final and non-final are never equivalent. Tap the cells that get an X now.
The only final state is D. Look for the pairs with D.
The three pairs with D. D is final, and the others are not.
Which of these tokens is a number? Tap it.
x1 has a digit, but it starts with a letter.
Ten. x1 is a name, because it starts with a letter.
In this grammar, which symbol will still be replaced by something else? Tap it.
It is the symbol on the left side of the rules.
E. It is on the left side, so it can be replaced.
In the tree, the deepest operation is done first. Tap the operator computed first.
Look for the operator farthest from the root.
Times. It is deeper, so it comes out first.
The rule E goes to T X becomes a function. Tap the line of code that starts that function.
The function has the name of the nonterminal.
void E. It calls T and then X, in the order of the rule.
n is on top, and there is the rule E goes to n. What does the parser do now? Tap it.
The top is already the whole right side of a rule.
Reduce. The n on top is a handle: n goes out and E comes in.
In the rule expr plus expr, each symbol has a number: dollar one, two and three. Which is the second expr? Tap it.
Count the plus too: it is a symbol.
Dollar three. The first expr is one, the plus is two, and the other expr is three.
a is int and x is float. And the two, with no point? Tap its type.
A number with no point has no decimal part.
Integer. A number written with no point has type int.
How many names appear in the line t2 equals a plus t1? Tap it.
Count the result and the two operands.
Three: t2, a and t1. The result and two operands.
fat of two is about to call fat of one. While fat of one runs, how many fat records are on the stack? Tap it.
fat of two has not finished yet.
Two. The record of fat of two is still there, waiting for the return.
Make it LL(1)
This grammar has both defects from the Bridge. The Temple parser chokes on it. Let us fix it in the textbook order.
First the recursion. Which line starts with its own nonterminal? Tap it.
Look for the rule whose right side starts with the same name as the left side.
The L line. L goes to L semicolon C starts with L itself.
1. no left recursion
L now goes to C and L prime. L prime repeats semicolon C, or vanishes. The sentences are the same.
Now the common prefix. Which line has two rules with the same start? Tap it.
Look at the first symbol of each rule, line by line.
The C line. Both rules start with id.
2. factored
Factored: C goes to id and C prime. C prime gets the rest of each rule: the equals with E, or the parentheses.
How many cells of the LL(1) table for this grammar get two rules? Tap it.
With no recursion and no repeated start, the parser always picks by the next token.
None. The grammar is now LL(1).
none
one
two
First remove the recursion, then factor. In the exam, show both grammars and say which defect each step fixed.
